title: Anaesthesia instruments: airway, laryngoscopes, needles, circuits
subject: Anesthesia
anchor: Name the instrument from its shape, then the one decisive use. Airway tools are graded by size; spinal vs epidural needles differ by tip and bevel.
Macintosh lifts the epiglottis indirectly (tip in vallecula); Miller lifts it directly (tip under epiglottis).

Tolerated in semi-conscious; avoid in base-of-skull fracture, coagulopathy
Elliptical cuff on a tube, sits over larynx
Supraglottic device; does not protect against aspiration; used in difficult airway rescue
Guide NG tube / ET tube; remove foreign body from pharynx
Difficult intubation: pass blindly then railroad tube

head: Item
Feature
Key fact

points: Spinal anaesthesia is given below L2 in adults (conus ends L1–L2); in children the cord ends lower (L3).
Epidural: Tuohy needle, loss of resistance to air or saline; test dose with lignocaine + adrenaline detects intravascular/intrathecal placement.
LMA is contraindicated when aspiration risk is high (full stomach, pregnancy).
Capnography is the gold-standard confirmation of ET tube placement (persistent waveform); chest rise and auscultation are supportive.
Pulse oximeter: red (660 nm) and infrared (940 nm) light; cannot tell CO-Hb apart from O2-Hb (reads falsely high).
Difficult airway: plan A intubation, B supraglottic (LMA), C face mask, D surgical airway (cricothyroidotomy).

traps.trap: Choose a Macintosh because it is the standard
traps.fix: Miller (straight) blade in infants: the epiglottis is long and floppy

traps.stem: Needle chosen for obstetric spinal to reduce headache
traps.trap: Quincke, because it is the thinnest
traps.fix: Pencil-point Whitacre/Sprotte; Quincke is a cutting tip with higher PDPH
Pulse oximeter reads COHb as oxyHb; check co-oximetry

cards.back: Macintosh (curved): vallecula. Miller (straight): lifts the epiglottis directly; used in infants.

points: Veress needle: spring-loaded blunt stylet; inserted at Palmer's point or umbilicus; pneumoperitoneum to 12–15 mmHg.

title: Obstetric and gynaecology instruments: forceps, speculum, vacuum, IUDs
subject: OBGY
anchor: Instrument OSCE: name, then 'used for', then one complication or contraindication.
Forceps: cephalic curve (fits head) and pelvic curve (fits birth canal); Kielland has minimal pelvic curve and sliding lock.

points: Forceps prerequisites: fully dilated cervix, ruptured membranes, engaged head, empty bladder, known position, adequate analgesia.
Ventouse: cup placed at flexion point 3 cm anterior to posterior fontanelle; pull ≤ 3 pulls and ≤ 20 minutes; avoid pop-offs >2.
Pap smear: sample the transformation zone with Ayre's spatula and cytobrush; fix immediately in 95% ethanol.
IUCD insertion best immediately after birth (<48 h), or after 4 weeks; Copper T failure ~0.8%/year (Pearl index).
Uterine perforation is the main hazard of sound, curette and IUCD insertion.

cards.back: Kielland forceps (sliding lock, minimal pelvic curve).

<34 weeks, face/brow, bleeding disorders, fetal macrosomia (relative).

title: ENT instruments: otoscope, tuning fork, speculums, tonsil set, tracheostomy
subject: ENT
anchor: ENT OSCE: identify the speculum/forceps and the orifice it opens.
Tuning fork 512 Hz for hearing tests (least overtones); 256/128 Hz for vibration.
points: Rinne: air conduction > bone conduction (AC > BC) = positive in normal/SNHL; negative in conductive loss.
Weber lateralises to the conductive ear or the good ear in SNHL.
Tracheostomy: incision at the 2nd–4th ring; thyroid isthmus divided; avoid first ring (subglottic stenosis).
Siegle speculum applies positive/negative pressure to test TM mobility.
Foreign body in nose of a child: unilateral foul discharge; remove with hook, not forceps pushing posteriorly.

cards.front: Frequency of tuning fork in clinics?

cards.back: Conductive loss ear; normal ear in SNHL.

title: Radiology and nuclear medicine equipment, dosimetry and protection
subject: Radiology
anchor: Equipment → principle → unit. Know which modality uses ionising radiation and the dosimeter for each situation.
TLD / film badge worn by staff; Geiger-Müller counter detects contamination.

tables.title: Equipment and detectors
head: Item
Principle
Fact
rows: Only ~1% energy becomes X-rays; 99% heat; rotating anode
TLD: LiF crystals emit light on heating
Personnel monitoring; TLD reusable, wider range
T1 fat bright; T2 fluid bright; no ionising radiation

points: Dose units: gray (absorbed), sievert (equivalent/effective = Gy × weighting factor); 1 Gy = 100 rad; 1 Sv = 100 rem.
Dose limits: public 1 mSv/yr; radiation worker 20 mSv/yr averaged over 5 years (AERB); pregnant worker 1 mSv to fetus for rest of pregnancy.
ALARA: time, distance (inverse square law), shielding.
Ultrasound: higher frequency = better resolution, less penetration.
MRI contraindications: pacemaker (older), cochlear implant, intracranial aneurysm clip (ferromagnetic), metallic foreign body in eye.

traps.fix: TLD / film badge; Geiger is for survey

cards.front: Annual dose limit for radiation worker?
cards.back: 20 mSv averaged over 5 years (max 30 in a year).

verify: AERB / ICRP dose limits (verify current year); half-lives standard
